newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Philippines Brady exchange bond widely distributed.
newsitem.headline: Philippines Brady exchange bond widely distributed.

text.p: The Philippines new 20-year fixed rate bond issued in exchange for Brady bonds attracted a geographically diverse investor base, lead manager J.P. Morgan said Friday.
Investors tendered US$678 million worth of collateralized bonds for the exchange programme. Of these, the Philippine government accepted US$635 million worth.
It also sold US$137 million new bonds to investors who did not have the old bonds to exchange but were willing to buy the bonds in cash, the Philippines announced Tuesday.
Of the investors that exchanged the bonds, 40 percent were from Asia, 35 percent from the U.S. and 25 percent from Europe, J.P. Morgan said.
Of those buying the bonds with new cash, 45 percent were from the U.S., 40 percent from Asia and 15 percent from Europe.

"As you would expect for the new money, there was a lot of U.S. interest because they are clearly interested in long maturity paper," said Richard Luddington, head of emerging market debt syndicate at J.P. Morgan in London.
But Luddington said the amount of new money demand coming from Asia for the 20-year paper was particularly significant.
"This is a very positive trend that reflects the increased willingness of Asian investors to go down the maturity curve to pick up yield," he said.
Investors included institutions, private accounts and banks.
